return.basis: The Medium and Large Greymanes and the Flagship wait on it.

effort.basis: A 320 m dive to one cave; the rest is luck.

name: Giant Hydrothermal Salamander Hide
summary: The Assault Ship of the East takes 10, and one comes only from killing and skinning a giant hydrothermal salamander. They live only at the Great Hydrothermal Vents, one or two at a time, so the hide is the slowest part of that build. Each also drops 1 to 3 Relics.

return.basis: The Assault Ship and the Giant Golden Compass Sail.

effort.basis: One creature, one site, one or two at a time.

name: Ambergris
summary: The Assault Ship of the East takes 10. Mine the glowing orange-yellow nodes on the Seabed Plain south of Delesyia, among the giant fish skeletons: 4 to 5 a node with the Knuckle Drill, so two or three nodes cover the build. Patch 2.05 added more nodes there. Pioneer Bergen Island and its dispatch pays some too.

return.basis: The Assault Ship and the large sterns.

effort.basis: Two or three nodes on one dive.

name: Camp Funds
summary: Every ship is paid in Camp Funds, and since patch 2.01 one donated Silver buys 1,000. That puts the Large Greymane's 500,000 at one Gold Bar exchanged at a bank, and a legendary's 750,000 at one and a half. Convert Silver as you need it rather than grinding missions.

effort.basis: Donated Silver; a Gold Bar is 500,000.

sources.title: DLC Shipbuilding Guide: All Ships and Upgrades — KeenGamer

methods.title: Gold Bars at a bank
methods.how: Exchange a Gold Bar at a bank and donate the Silver: 500,000 Camp Funds.

methods.title: Money dispatches
methods.how: Excavation and exploration missions pay Camp Funds while you sail.

name: Camp Stock
summary: Builds draw Stone, Timber and Provisions from the camp's stockpile, not your bag: 600 of each for the first ship, 45,000 Stone and Timber and 90,000 Provisions for a legendary. Supply dispatches refill all three while you're at sea; donations top them up.

return.basis: Every built ship waits on it.

effort.basis: Supply dispatches and donations.

sources.title: DLC Shipbuilding Guide: All Ships and Upgrades — KeenGamer

methods.title: Supply dispatches
methods.how: Keep quarries, logging camps, farms and fishing docks on repeat.

methods.title: Donate to Carl
methods.how: Donate ore, timber and food; each becomes camp stock.

name: Comrades
summary: A build is a dispatch: it ties up comrades until it finishes. The first ship takes 5 with one Engineering skill among them, the Large Greymane 20, a legendary 10. Grey-0 workers fill the ordinary places so your named Greymanes stay free for other missions.

return.basis: Every built ship waits on them.

effort.basis: Recruit and keep enough idle comrades.

sources.title: How Do You Get, Build, and Upgrade Ships — Whisper of the House

methods.title: Free up comrades

name: Outfitter Parts
summary: The quickest speed gain in the game is a sail. The Delesyian, Tidesworn and Demenissian Sails each add 2 Speed and 100 Health for 110 to 275 Silver by hull size; fit one at a Ship Manager the day you get a new hull.

return.basis: Speed for every hull you own.

effort.basis: A shop stop.

sources.title: DLC Shipbuilding Guide: All Ships and Upgrades — KeenGamer

name: Hidden Ship Blueprints
trait: Sails and sterns no shop sells
summary: The best parts are found, not bought. The Giant Golden Compass Sail's manual sits behind a waterfall at Castaway's Shelter on Ocula Island; the Steam and Clockwork Stern and Figurehead share a chest in sunken ruins west of Iliya Island. Craft them at a Workstation, then fit them at a Ship Manager.

return.basis: The fastest fittings for medium, large and giant hulls.

effort.basis: Two hidden chests, then a Workstation bill.

name: Build, Don't Buy
trait: Saves 5.5 million and two speed steps
summary: Every Greymane build is faster and cheaper than the hull a Ship Manager sells at its size. The Medium Greymane costs 100,000 against 1,200,000 and the Large 500,000 against 6,000,000, and both are two Movement steps quicker. Buy a large hull only for its 36-slot hold.

return.basis: Saves 5,630,000 Camp Funds across the three sizes.

effort.basis: The Greymane builds' ocean materials.

name: Island Pioneering
trait: Opens the dispatches that farm for you
summary: Pioneering an island is a dispatch from its anchorage, and it opens the island's own missions. Three matter to a fleet: Auronui for the Ship Teleportation Device blueprint, Iliya for Natural Pearls, Bergen for Ambergris. Do them in that order, as soon as you can sail.

return.basis: Turns three islands into passive material income.

effort.basis: Comrades and in-game hours.

sources.title: How to Get the Drunken Catfish Legendary Galleon — FinalBoss
Ambergris — Vulkk
Natural Pearl — Vulkk

methods.title: Auronui first
methods.how: Three comrades, 12 hours; its buried treasure is the Ship Teleportation Device blueprint.

methods.title: Iliya next
methods.how: FinalBoss: four comrades, 18 hours. It opens the Ruins Excavation dispatch, the pearl farm.

methods.title: Bergen
methods.how: Opens a dispatch with a chance at Ambergris.

tips.text: Pass time at a campfire to finish a pioneering dispatch sooner.

name: Island Dispatches
trait: Pearls and Ambergris while you sail
summary: A pioneered island gives its own dispatches, and two of them farm what legendary ships need. Iliya's Ruins Excavation pays Natural Pearls and Bergen's mission pays Ambergris, neither on every run. Deckhands work the island development missions. Keep both running from the day you pioneer them.

return.basis: Pearls and Ambergris without a dive.

effort.basis: Free comrades and repeat sends.

name: Crew Roles
trait: The jobs that sail without you
summary: A crew works the ship while you don't: First Mate, Rigger and Lookout are needed to leave port, Gunners fire, Carpenters repair, Deckhands fish at anchor and run island missions. Roles change only in port, so set them before every voyage.

return.basis: Repairs, fire and fishing without you at the wheel.

effort.basis: Assign at a Ship Manager.

name: Sea Hauling
trait: 36 slots of trade goods a voyage
summary: A ship's hold carries trade goods and nothing else: 6 slots on a rowboat up to 36 on a bought large hull. The DLC added sea trade goods for maritime routes, but no guide has published a route's profit yet. Haul only with a large hull, and treat the voyage as a bonus on a trip you were making anyway.

return.basis: No source publishes a sea route's profit.

effort.basis: A 6,000,000 hull for the big hold.
